excerpt: Station was a Paris-built desktop app that put all your work web apps in one window. The company is listed as inactive and getstation.com no longer hosts it, but the app's open-source code is still on GitHub.
content:
Station was a desktop app for Mac, Windows and Linux that gathered the web apps you use for work, such as Gmail, Slack, Trello, Google Drive and Notion, into a single window. Instead of dozens of browser tabs, each app sat as an icon in a sidebar, with one search bar across all of them, a combined notifications feed and a focus mode that silenced notifications for a while. TechCrunch described it as a sort of Spotlight for web apps.

Station was built inside eFounders, the Paris startup studio now called Hexa. Hexa's company page says it was known at first as BrowserX, joined the studio's 2017 batch and launched publicly in 2017; it names Julien Berthomier and Alexandre Lachèze as the team. Station took part in Y Combinator's Winter 2018 batch. In May 2018 Tech.eu reported that the Paris-based company raised €3.25 million (reported by others as $3.25 million) for what it called a browser for work, designed to cut distractions and tab overload.

No longer active as a company. Both Y Combinator's directory and Hexa's portfolio page now list Station as inactive, and Y Combinator's profile describes its later pivot towards a team knowledge base. The getstation.com domain no longer hosts Station; when we checked it redirected to an unrelated site, so we do not link to it. The desktop app's source code remains public on GitHub under the Apache 2.0 licence, and the repository was still receiving updates in October 2026.

If you want an app like this today, look at the alternatives below. This profile draws on Station's GitHub repository and published reporting. We have not tested the app, and nothing here is paid placement.
